acceptanceCriteria: corpusindex.Open and doccorpus.ParseArtifact allocation no longer depends on the json/v2 pooled-encoder state: TotalAlloc across GOMAXPROCS=1, default and GOGC=10 runs varies by less than 10% (numbers retained), measured with the V1-0587 phase bracket
The ordinary-run TotalAlloc of TestCorpusIndex... (internal/corpusindex index_test.go ceiling test) stays at least 25% under the unchanged 1 GiB ceiling at GOGC=10, run ids or local numbers retained
Encoded bytes are identical before and after (digest of the corpus/index artifacts compared on the live repository); no ceiling or race guard is relaxed
body: Found by the V1-0587 lane (PR #895, build log docs/build-log/2026-10-14-v1-0587-corpus-alloc-ceiling.md; darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.2). corpusindex.Open (about 658 MB of a 768 MB ordinary run) and doccorpus.ParseArtifact (110 to 270 MB) marshal the 30 to 35 MB corpus or index several times. Measured: one json/v2 Marshal of the 29.8 MB corpus costs 190,565,456 bytes (61 mallocs) on a cold pooled encoder versus 29,818,880 bytes (1 malloc) warm, and TotalAlloc moves in exact steps of that 160,746,576-byte difference. Whether the encoder is warm depends on GC count, the per-P pool slot and race-mode Put drops, so allocation varies with GOMAXPROCS, GOGC and -race: ordinary default 767.7 to 957.3 MB; GOGC=10 reached 1,115,746,416 bytes (over the 1 GiB test ceiling); hosted linux/amd64 race runs 1.09 to 1.41 GB. Expected: allocation roughly proportional to output size and stable across runtime settings. Suggested direction (from the lane, not measured): MarshalWrite into a pre-grown bytes.Buffer and removal of duplicate re-encodes. The host-load-to-GC link is inferred, not traced.
title: corpusindex/doccorpus: repeated json/v2 marshals of the 30 MB corpus cost up to 6.4x output on a cold pooled encoder, making allocation GC- and GOMAXPROCS-dependent
